clue.text: Sharp, tiny boy in unit

indicators.note: in places the small boy's name within the word for a unit

parts.note: one is a unit, the single whole number
Tim is a short boy's name, tiny as in Tiny Tim

explanation.surface: A small lad is described as quick-witted while serving in a military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at three o'clock sharp means arriving punctually, exactly at the stated hour.

clue.text: Subject to conditions, released one about polar wandering

indicators.note: about means the word for one goes around the other letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so the word polar is rearranged

explanation.surface: A prisoner let out early is said to be wandering around the polar regions.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner freed early under supervision, liable to recall if terms are broken, is released on licence in this way.

clue.text: Nip nipper

definitions.meaning: a nip is a small drink of spirits, a dram
a nipper is a small child, informally

explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of whisky and a toddler share this short word.

clue.text: Modus operandi to free policeman

parts.note: MO is the standard abbreviation for modus operandi, a method of working
to untie is to free from bonds

explanation.surface: A police procedure involving releasing someone from custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Royal Canadian Mounted Police is known by this nickname.

clue.text: Careless fielders keep dropping Leicestershire's opener

parts.note: slips are cricket fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper

indicators.note: dropping means a letter is taken out of the word for keep

parts.note: to keep is to hold

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes in first

explanation.surface: Sloppy cricket fielders keep letting catches slip off Leicestershire's opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIPS are close catchers in cricket; Leicestershire is an English county side. HOLD loses its L to give HOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is slapdash and careless, done without proper attention.

clue.text: Later, illnesses spread in a group of Caribbean islands

indicators.note: illnesses spread around, so the letters of the two words are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Diseases later spread through a Caribbean island chain.
explanation.definitionFit: This chain, including Barbados and Trinidad, is a named group in the eastern Caribbean.

clue.text: Light-hearted drama, very abridged

parts.note: a play is a drama

indicators.note: abridged means shortened, so the last letter of the word for very is dropped

parts.note: full can mean very, as in 'full well'

explanation.surface: A comic drama that has been heavily cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-hearted and playful both describe a mood that is fun-loving and not serious.

clue.text: A legislature with all the answers?

definitions.text: A legislature with all the answers?

parts.words: A legislature with all the answers?
parts.note: the Isle of Man's parliament chamber, read whimsically as a building full of keys, that is, solutions

explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man's lower chamber has this name; keys are also answer sheets to puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx parliament's elected chamber bears this name, and keys are solutions, hence all the answers.

clue.text: Uncover man, decapitated writer, inside

indicators.note: inside places the shortened writer within the word for a man

parts.note: dude is slang for a man

indicators.note: decapitated means losing the head, the first letter of the word for writer

parts.note: a pen is a writer, the instrument one writes with

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a man and a beheaded author found within.
explanation.definitionFit: To denude is to strip bare, removing a covering.

clue.text: Very fast (too fast), a tanker at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the fodder are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tanker steaming much too fast while at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Going at a great speed, from the nautical knot as a unit of speed; an idiom for rapidly.

clue.text: Set sail, and disconcert sailor during meal

parts.note: to put out is to disconcert or upset

indicators.note: during means the sailor comes inside the meal

parts.note: tea is a meal
OS stands for ordinary seaman, a sailor

explanation.surface: A ship sets off and a sailor is upset during his tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that leaves harbour for open water sets sail; the phrasal verb means departing by sea.

clue.text: What could be held by mourner?

definitions.text: What could be held by mourner?

indicators.note: held by means the letters are found within the word mourner

explanation.surface: A grieving person at a funeral carries something.
explanation.definitionFit: A mourner may carry a vessel holding the ashes of the dead.

clue.text: Very amusing short word for a seismologist

parts.note: rich means very amusing, as in 'that's rich'

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for word is cut off

parts.note: a term is a word

explanation.surface: A funny word to describe an earthquake scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Richter, the American seismologist, devised the scale measuring earthquake magnitude.

clue.text: Bargains to be had here, offered by a saloon-keeper?

definitions.text: Bargains to be had here, offered by a saloon-keeper?

parts.words: Bargains to be had here, offered by a saloon-keeper?
parts.note: a saloon is a car, and the part of it that keeps luggage is the boot, so its goods are sold from there

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saloon-keeper' suggests a barman; the saloon is a car, whose boot holds things. In Britain people sell second-hand goods from car boots at these events.
explanation.definitionFit: This British event is a market where people sell secondhand goods cheaply from their vehicles.

clue.text: Death closes terrible life in London borough

indicators.note: closes means the word for death encloses the other letters

parts.note: death is the end

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of life are mangled

explanation.surface: Death brings a terrible life to its close.
explanation.walkthrough: ENFIELD is a borough in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfield is one of the boroughs of Greater London, in the north.

clue.text: Very imposing — that's how actors are on the cinema screen

definitions.meaning: a figure who is flamboyant and dramatic in personality

definitions.text: that's how actors are on the cinema screen
definitions.meaning: literally, film projection shows actors bigger than real people

explanation.definitionFit: Exaggerated and flamboyant people seem bigger than ordinary, and screen images are literally oversized.

clue.text: Exploits accepted of French undergraduates

indicators.note: accepted means the outer word takes in the French word

parts.note: stunts are exploits, daring feats
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Daring exploits by French students.
explanation.definitionFit: Undergraduates are university students who have not yet taken a first degree.

clue.text: Show optimism flogging her beef hotpots

indicators.note: flogging beats the letters around, so her beef hotpots is rearranged

explanation.surface: A cook trying to sell beef hotpots.
explanation.definitionFit: To be optimistic is to expect a good outcome; this idiom means hoping things turn out well.

clue.text: Showed nitrogen stored in odd device

indicators.note: stored in means the nitrogen symbol is put inside
odd signals the letters of device are rearranged

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Nitrogen kept inside a strange gadget was put on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or reveal a feeling or quality plainly.

clue.text: Display stand in entrance, brought up before

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: A display stand at the entrance was carried up first.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a set of open shelves for displaying ornaments.

clue.text: Completely at home, Dorothy Gale's dog

parts.note: in means at home
Toto is Dorothy's dog in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: A Wizard of Oz reference: the dog is home again.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means as a whole or entirely.

clue.text: Make petty criticisms in police station about parking behind it

indicators.note: about means the police station goes around the other letters

parts.note: nick is British slang for a police station

indicators.note: behind means the parking letter comes after the other word

parts.note: taken as written
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A complaint at the police station about parking behind the building.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for a police station (or prison).
explanation.definitionFit: To nitpick is to find fault over trivial details.

clue.text: Worked together with one in LA, one's editor

indicators.note: in puts the first numeral inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written: Los Angeles
I is the Roman numeral for one
one's gives I plus S, read as 'one is'

explanation.surface: Someone collaborated with a person in Los Angeles who works as an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to cooperate and communicate as partners; the past tense means cooperated.

clue.text: Star losing face in cells

indicators.note: losing face means the first letter of the word for star is removed

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: A star humiliated while locked in prison cells.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova are egg cells, female reproductive cells.

clue.text: When there is no shooting nearby, a boy crosses Seine's banks

parts.note: close means nearby

indicators.note: banks are the edges, so the outer letters of Seine's are used

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy crosses the banks of the Seine in Paris when the hunting stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crosses' sets A SON beside SE, as if walking over the river's banks. A close season is the period when shooting game is banned.
explanation.definitionFit: During the closed period for game the law forbids hunting, so no shooting takes place.

clue.text: Consult bishop's office

definitions.meaning: to ... a doctor is to consult one
a diocese, the seat or jurisdiction of a bishop

explanation.definitionFit: One consults a specialist by visiting them, and a bishop's diocese is called his see.

clue.text: Take too much round Cape, having very large load

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: having ... load means the island name carries the size inside it

parts.note: Cape stands for Cape Verde, the island nation
OS is outsize, very large in clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A ship rounds the Cape with an oversized cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like a headland to sail round, but it is short for Cape Verde, the island nation off West Africa; 'having ... load' makes it carry the size inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdose is to take an excessive amount of a drug.

clue.text: Engineers' former tax break

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps
cess was an old tax or levy

explanation.surface: Army engineers get a historic tax break.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a break from work, as when parliament stops sitting.
